subject: Consolidated offer matrix + co-sell routing: regionization & packaging decisions

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, sarah.connors@amazon.com, paul.kim@microsoft.com, gcp-partner@sales.google.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated offer matrix + co-sell routing: regionization & packaging decisions

Team / partners —

Thanks for jumping on this thread. Attached is v3 of the offer matrix (redwood_offer_matrix_v3.xlsx) — it contains a first pass at SKUs we can publish per cloud, suggested region launches, and packaging options (PAYG, committed reserved, Dedicated bundles). We need to converge on a recommended pattern so Marketplace ops can create the first listings and enable co-sell workflows.

High-level asks:
- Finalize which SKUs go live on AWS, Azure, GCP for the initial program (we can stagger regions).
- Confirm packaging semantics: (a) Marketplace PAYG (hosted API), (b) Dedicated/Reserved only via private quoting, (c) Private/VPC as BYOL or \"private SaaS\" offer.
- Define co-sell enablement triggers (e.g., ARR threshold, integration milestone, joint customer qualification).
- Agree a regional priority list (US / EU / APAC) and specific regions for cloud listing (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast1).

Timeline: marketplace ops needs a decision by EOD Wed 16 Jun so we can get the canary listing into AWS and Azure by the 3rd week of June.

Notes for external partners: Sarah/Paul/GCP partner — please flag any marketplace constraints on your side (naming, offer types, required SKUs).

Attachments: redwood_offer_matrix_v3.xlsx (attachment)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_marketplace_offers

Thanks,
Lauren

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated offer matrix + co-sell routing: regionization & packaging decisions

Agree with the ask — a few practical suggestions from listing ops perspective: 

1) Launch cadence: start with a minimal set of offers per cloud — Hosted API PAYG + an \"Entry Dedicated\" SKU for predictable throughput. Leave the full Dedicated bundles out of Marketplace on day one (we can handle via reserved capacity contracts).

2) Regions (initial canary):
   - AWS: us-east-1, eu-west-1
   - Azure: west europe, east us
   - GCP: us-central1, europe-west1
These cover sales coverage and co-sell partner regions. If APAC demand spikes, add asia-northeast1 / asia-southeast1 in phase 2.

3) Naming / offer types: marketplaces require consistent naming and SKU IDs. I'm attaching a short doc with recommended naming conventions and the offer_type mapping we should use. We should avoid packaging the Dedicated product as a marketplace-managed entitlement — that creates procurement complexity for enterprise customers.

Attachment: marketplace_naming_convention.docx

On the co-sell side, we should bake in a metatag so marketplace leads are routed to the regional AE by default and flag any \"strategic\" accounts for partner co-sell.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — a few procurement / pricing constraints to call out before we lock SKUs: 

- Pricing floors: enterprise procurement teams often require a PO/commit for Dedicated / Reserved capacity. If we publish Dedicated as a marketplace SKU, customers will try to check out — that will trigger procurement that requires SOWs and special SLAs. Recommend leaving Dedicated as quote-only and exposing only PAYG and "committed credits" bundles on marketplace.

- Packaging tiers: propose three visible marketplace tiers: Starter (PAYG, low rate limit), Growth (PAYG + moderate committed credits), Enterprise (quote-only, contact sales). This keeps the catalogue simple for self-serve and preserves sales motion for bigger deals.

- Legal redlines: marketplace contracts in EU require data residency disclosures per region; we should annotate each offer with a residency field. I'll follow up with legal on standard clauses but wanted to flag this as it affects copy and listing metadata.

Attachment: procurement_constraints_summary.pdf

A couple operational items we should decide now so co-sell routing works out of the gate: 

- Lead flow: map marketplace leads to HubSpot. Use a marketplace offer tag to derive region and initial lead owner. I'll create HubSpot workflows that assign the AE by region and tag \"marketplace_inbound\".

- Co-sell criteria: suggest we enable co-sell when: ARR >= $50k OR integration depth (direct connect / private networking) is required. For anything above that we route to a Partner AE and loop in partner contact.

- Telemetry / attribution: marketplace will only send limited telemetry. We need to set up a lead enrichment job to append the marketplace metadata to HubSpot (offer_id, region, cloud). This will let Growth/CS measure conversion.

See attached quick playbook (co-sell-playbook_v1.md) for initial workflows.

Marcus
Head of GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — good alignment. Summarizing decisions and owners so ops can move quickly: 

Decisions (final):
- Initial marketplace offers per cloud:
  * Hosted API PAYG (AWS, Azure, GCP) — available in us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast1 (canary in us-east-1 / eu-west-1).
  * Committed credit bundles (PAYG + committed credits) visible on marketplace for Starter and Growth tiers (self-serve).
  * Dedicated / Reserved bundles: quote-only, handled by Redwood sales (not published as purchasable SKUs).
- Naming & metadata: use Jonas' naming conventions document; include data residency metadata per offer (Karthik to lead legal copy).
- Co-sell routing: Marketplace leads -> HubSpot mapping (Marcus to build workflows). Co-sell enabled when ARR >= $50k or when private networking is requested.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Lauren: update offer matrix to v4, push to Drive; create canary listing plan for AWS us-east-1 and Azure west europe. Due: Fri 18 Jun.
- Jonas: prepare final listing spec (offer names, SKU IDs) and handoff to listing ops. Due: Wed 16 Jun EOD.
- Karthik: provide legal copy for EU data residency and confirm procurement guidance for marketplace copy. Due: Thu 17 Jun.
- Marcus: publish HubSpot workflows and lead enrichment job. Due: Mon 21 Jun.

Attachments: redwood_offer_matrix_v4.xlsx
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_marketplace_offers

If there are no objections, I'll push v4 and signal ops to start the canary next week.

Thanks,
Lauren
